title: How worried should we be about the invasive mosquitoes in the UK? | New Scientist
description: Invasive mosquitoes that can carry viruses like dengue, chikungunya and Zika have been found breeding in east London
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Super El Niño could have unexpected effect on UK winter | New Scientist
description: An El Niño is usually expected to herald a cold end to winter in the UK – but this year could be different
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Lucid dreams induced via multisensory stimulation | New Scientist
description: Lucid dreams, when a person is aware they're dreaming and can often control them, could be induced in people who rarely experience them
author: Emma Young

title: Nations and big tech to train AI using ‘gold dust’ data from Ukraine | New Scientist
description: Foreign states and technology firms are scrambling for data from the Ukraine war so they can train the next-generation of AI models that might be used in defence and national security
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Pig kidney kept a man off dialysis for nine months in world first | New Scientist
description: A pig kidney transplant worked for a record nine months. This enabled the recipient to stay off dialysis for longer while waiting for a suitable human donor's kidney to become available
author: Chris Simms

title: Psilocybin could prevent common and debilitating chemotherapy side effect | New Scientist
description: Many people who have chemotherapy develop numbness, tingling and pain in their hands and feet, which can disrupt their treatment. But research suggests that psilocybin, the psychedelic in magic mushrooms, could prevent this side effect
author: Carissa Wong
